rv.q: With its compassionate and honest handling of nonbinary visibility, it elevates the piece beyond flashy costumes and big tap numbers.
Olney’s production comes as close to perfection as one could ask for an opening night in a renewed theater space.

Helmed by out artistic director Jason Loewith, OTC’s exhilarating production is brimming with fun, feeling, and the musical’s focus on Black identity and gender exploration (recreated for Broadway by writers Matthew López /Amber Ruffin, and songwriting team Marc Schaiman/Scott Whittman).
The whole evening was entertaining and thrilling, and the production was a sparkling as the champagne we drank to celebrate the occasion.

cn.t: Critics praise this "sizzling" and "big, brassy" production as a fitting debut for Olney's renovated theatre, with the Tony-winning musical adaptation successfully bringing showbiz spectacle to the new space.
